note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: What boiler service and control functions apply, and what do existing records establish about any applicable steam-water level-control basis?

where: site records: permitted existing equipment/service description and design/control narrative identifying heat source, water/steam service, drum or no-drum configuration, intended operating modes and source revision/owner
data_requests.how: Establish boiler service and applicability before any drum task. A boiler name alone does not establish a steam-water drum. For supplied hot-water or other no-drum service, acknowledge the applicable scope instead of imposing drum-control work. Unknown service requires clarification, not an inferred missing controller. Unfired waste-heat steam-drum equipment may still need level-control review despite having no fuel or combustion scope.

data_requests.item: Applicable control configuration, operating modes and review disposition
where: site records: existing design/control narratives and operating evidence for the functions actually applicable to this boiler; where steam-water level control applies, retain level, steam-flow and feedwater-flow relationships and normal/startup/low-load modes
DCS/PLC configuration: applicable approved existing controller, measurement/output and mode records, through the company-approved access route
data_requests.how: Keep indication labels distinct from configured and active control. S8 describes level-only and additional steam/feedwater-flow inputs, including response to abrupt load changes; it does not mandate three-element control on every boiler. Review intended normal/startup/low-load modes and relevant load/feedwater conditions without declaring a single-element mode faulty. Adequate existing evidence may settle or defer the job without a project; new work belongs to the responsible company reviewer.

questions.decision_rule: First establish service and applicable control functions. Review combustion only where relevant; review steam-water level control only where that service applies, including waste-heat steam-drum equipment without a burner. Three depicted measurements do not prove an active three-element loop, and a missing depicted element does not establish an upgrade need. Existing supported design/mode and operating records may answer or defer the investigation; retain unresolved evidence and next owner.

typical_benefit.wording: S8 describes boiler combustion and water-level control functions and differing levels of control complexity. S19’s historical broad boiler process-control estimate is not a three-element drum-control gain; no percentage or payback is assigned to this applicability review.
source_titles: S8: Improving Steam System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 2nd ed. (DOE/GO-102012-3423, rev. Oct 2012)
S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: C5 uses S8 printed6–7/PDFindices11–12 explicitly for boiler functional/service review. The boiler selector does not infer a drum, combustion or missing control; dry furnaces/kilns are outside this boiler-specific question and may use E16 where eligible. Unfired waste-heat steam-drum equipment remains eligible without fuel evidence. S19/S24 do not establish a universal three-element requirement or drum-specific benefit. Supplied Boolean/service/qualification fields are literal claims, not installed-state, adequate performance or company authority.
